content: <element1><element2>Website accounts and email</element2><element3><element4>When you register, we process the submitted display name, email address, irreversible password hash, email-verification status, and account-creation time.</element4><element4>After sign-in, PostgreSQL stores the website account and database sessions. A session contains a random token, expiry, IP address, and browser identifier used for security decisions. Plain-text passwords are never stored.</element4><element4>For email verification and password reset, the email address, message body, and necessary delivery metadata are sent to Resend. Email verification codes expire after <element5>10</element5> minutes and password-reset links after one hour.</element4><element4>Account information is retained until you delete the account or it must be removed by law. Sessions remain until expiry, sign-out, password reset, suspension, or revocation. Account deletion removes the account, all sessions, and associated business data.</element4><element4>After sign-in, automatic synchronization of the MAA Box, layout, settings, limited workspace versions, and schedule history begins only after you accept the current policies. Until then, or if you decline, the site remains in local-only mode.</element4><element4>Each MAA Box is protected with an independent data key and AES-<element5>256</element5>-GCM envelope encryption. The master key exists only in server configuration and is not written to the database, logs, or backups. Layouts and schedule results are allowlisted before storage.</element4><element4>At most <element5>10</element5> cloud workspace versions are retained for up to <element5>30</element5> days. At most <element5>5</element5> ordinary schedules are retained on a rolling <element5>30</element5>-day basis, and up to <element5>5</element5> may be pinned for long-term storage.</element4><element4>You may withdraw synchronization consent or delete cloud data. This removes the workspace, encrypted Box, schedule history, and related cache references. A sanitized local copy may remain in the browser if you choose.</element4>{choice1, select, yes {<element4>The Skland account-binding table stores only a pseudonymous binding value, the associated website user and authorization time, not Skland UID, display name, Box or credentials. Task inputs and reproduction records are described separately below; this does not mean that no business processing stores an Operator Box.</element4>} other {}}</element3></element1><element1><element2>Voluntary feedback and reproduction records</element2><element3><element4>Feedback and its private reproduction snapshot are saved only when you explicitly select the consent checkbox and submit the feedback form.</element4><element4>The snapshot includes the calculation diagnostic ID, base layout, submitted Operator Box, rotation settings and count, Fiammetta enablement and source type. Room reports also include a room summary; performance reports include calculation duration.</element4><element4>These records are available only to administrators for reproduction and troubleshooting, not in public feedback responses, product pages, analytics or ordinary logs, and are retained for at most <element5>30</element5> days.</element4><element4>Deleting a website account deletes associated feedback and reproduction records. Deleting all Skland data deletes snapshots linkable to that Skland account. Use the contact channels in this policy for other early deletion requests.</element4></element3></element1><element1><element2>Experience analytics and device information</element2><element3><element4>First-party experience analytics automatically record allowlisted events such as page views, schedule requests and rendering, Web Vitals, long tasks, and front-end errors. There is currently no separate opt-out, and no third-party analytics SDK is used.</element4><element4>A randomly generated stable analytics-session identifier is saved in localStorage to associate events from the same browser. “Clear local data” removes it; a new identifier is generated on a later visit.</element4><element4>A record may contain server receipt time, page route, precise duration in milliseconds or an integer metric, and allowlisted environment fields such as device type, operating system, browser category, screen size, pixel ratio, memory, processor-core count, and network type. Full User-Agent strings, request bodies, MAA Boxes, and login credentials are not stored.</element4><element4>When signed in, events are associated with the website user ID. If the browser also has an active Skland account, events are associated with an irreversible HMAC derived from the upstream account identifier. Skland UID, display name, Box, full status, and tokens are not written.</element4><element4>Detailed events expire <element5>30</element5> days after server receipt and are deleted during later writes and server maintenance. Deleting a website account cascades to events associated with that account. Unassociated browser events remain until expiry.</element4><element4>Network addresses are used for same-origin checks and rate limiting but are not stored in the application event table. Analytics requests and error logs contain only minimum diagnostic fields, not event bodies.</element4></element3></element1>{choice1, select, yes {<element1><element6>1. Scope and operator</element6><element7>This policy applies to “Closure Infrastructure Terminal” (the “site”), an unofficial, non-commercial scheduling assistant with no affiliation, agency relationship, or endorsement from Hypergryph, Skland, or the official Arknights project.</element7><element7>Operator: <value15></value15>. Contact us through the <element9>project issue tracker</element9>{choice2, select, yes { or <element10><value11></value11></element10>} other {}}.</element7></element1><element1><element6>2. Information we process</element6><element12>Scheduling data</element12><element3><element4>Credentials, tokens, device identifiers, and upstream user identifiers produced by Skland QR-code or credential import.</element4><element4>Bound characters, operator ownership and progression, base facilities, current assignments, morale, production recipes, and trading orders.</element4><element4>Imported MAA JSON, compatible spreadsheets, layout settings, and generated schedules.</element4></element3><element12>Full status-center data</element12><element7>After you accept this policy and sign in, the site directly reads full status information—including avatar, UID, level, sanity, missions, recruitment, outfits, training, clues, events, and game progress—and displays fields supported by the interface. No separate status-center authorization is required.</element7><element12>Necessary technical information</element12><element7>For API security and troubleshooting, the site briefly processes request ID, time, route, error code, response status, and network address forwarded by a proxy. Logs do not contain request bodies or login credentials.</element7></element1><element1><element6>3. Processing and purposes</element6><element3><element4>Login credentials are encrypted with AES-<element5>256</element5>-GCM and stored in this browser as an HttpOnly cookie. They are decrypted by the server during requests and are not written to the business database.</element4><element4>Raw credential text exists only briefly in component memory and for one request. After success it is cleared immediately and is not written to localStorage, sessionStorage, telemetry, logs, or the database.</element4><element4>To distinguish a bound account from a currently valid browser credential, The account-binding table stores an HMAC derived from the upstream Skland account identifier, the associated website user, and authorization time. That table does not store Skland UID, display name, Box or tokens.</element4><element4>Credentials are used only to synchronize character data, switch characters, and refresh a Skland session. The site does not read, store, or display inventory materials, sign in automatically, or post, like, or operate community content.</element4><element4>The Skland player-information API returns combined data. After sign-in, the server derives a minimum scheduling snapshot and a full-status allowlist. The raw response is not returned to the browser; full-status snapshots remain only in page memory and are not persisted in the browser or server run records.</element4><element4>Operator and layout data are sent to the site’s solver to generate rotations, efficiency summaries, and MAA exports.</element4></element3></element1><element1><element6>4. Retention</element6><element3><element4>Skland credentials are stored for a fixed <element5>7</element5> days after a successful scan or import. Reloading the page or refreshing a token does not extend this period.</element4><element4>A Skland binding remains until you sign out that account, delete all Skland data, or delete the website account. Seven days after the latest authorization it is marked “renewal required”, and authorization must be repeated before synchronization.</element4><element4>Server CLI run records and private feedback reproduction snapshots are retained for at most <element5>30</element5> days and may be deleted earlier.</element4><element4>Browser layouts, Operator Boxes, and recent schedules are normally retained for at most <element5>30</element5> days. “Delete all Skland data” immediately removes Skland-sourced content from them.</element4><element4>Incomplete QR-code login records are retained for at most <element5>10</element5> minutes.</element4></element3></element1><element1><element6>5. Third-party services</element6><element7>QR-code sign-in, credential validation, and character synchronization send requests to Skland and Hypergryph login services and are governed by the <element13>Skland License and Service Agreement</element13> and <element14>Skland Personal Information Protection Policy</element14>. The site does not sell your information or use credentials for purposes outside this policy.</element7></element1><element1><element6>6. Your choices and rights</element6><element3><element4>You may use MAA JSON or a compatible file without signing in to Skland.</element4><element4>You may sign out the current Skland account and remove its website-account binding at any time.</element4><element4>“Delete all Skland data” removes all login credentials, synchronized data, and linkable server records. It does not delete your official Skland account.</element4><element4>To access, correct, or remove information that cannot be deleted through the page, use the contact channel in this policy.</element4></element3></element1><element1><element6>7. Minors</element6><element7>If you are a minor under applicable law, use Skland synchronization only after a guardian has read and accepted this policy. A guardian may contact us to request deletion.</element7></element1><element1><element6>8. Security and changes</element6><element7>The site uses measures including HTTPS, HttpOnly cookies, same-origin checks, rate limiting, field allowlists, and minimal logging. No internet service can guarantee absolute security.
